published_statement: NOT QUOTED VERBATIM: the primary was not read by this agent. As carried from the sibling audit's at-source reading of L03 Table 3 (p.1225), the CI group weighted means in ppm are H 21015, C 35180, N 2940 +- 20, O 458200, Na 5010, Mg 95870, Al 8500, Si 106500, P 920 +- 100, S 54100, Cl 704, K 530, Ca 9070, Fe 182800, Ni 10640, Zn 310, As 1.73 +- 0.06, Li 1.46. The same relay says these are means over the Alais, Ivuna, Orgueil, Revelstoke and Tonk analyses available by 2003, with parenthesised outliers excluded. This agent confirms none of it independently.
published_hypotheses: H1 (carried, sibling audit H7): the CI value for each element is a weighted mean over the analyses available by 2003 of five CI falls (Alais, Ivuna, Orgueil, Revelstoke, Tonk), with outliers excluded. So it is an average for a meteorite group, not a measurement of any asteroid.

H2 (carried): each element has its own uncertainty, P +-100 ppm (about 11%) and N +-20 ppm. Compilations disagree on how uncertain N is: MS95 labels N 'F2' (a factor of 2, READ from the pyrolite file); PON14 gives 2 sigma = 885 ppm (READ from the pyrolite file); LBP25 gives +-970 (carried) or +-447 (search snippet).

H3 (standard in the CI literature, NOT READ in L03 here): CI chondrites match the solar photosphere for the condensable elements, but are depleted in the most volatile ones (H, C, N, O, noble gases) and differ for Li. The CI/solar ratios computed from the tree's own tables (section 7 of the re-derivation) agree: N x0.0285, C x0.092, H x0.0002, P x1.11.

H4: the numbers are mass fractions of bulk meteorite, including water and organics. The table is a composition, and says nothing on whether that composition is accessible, how much of it there is, or where it sits in the Solar System.
hypothesis_drift: ATTRIBUTION DISCREPANCY (in the tree, not in Lodders). stockgate.py:284-285 SOURCES['L03'] and stock.py:195 SOURCES['chondrite'] credit the CHONDRITE table (stockgate.py:395-414; stock.py:216-219) to L03, but the table is not L03 Table 3. Against the carried L03 values, only 7 of 39 elements agree within 0.5% (Si, S, Ca, Na, F, Ga, Ag). Against McDonough & Sun 1995 (READ), 19 of 58 agree within 0.5% (Si, Mg, S, C, Al, N, Cr, Pb, Ba, Rb, Li, Mo, Ag, Cs, Sb, Au, Tl, Bi, In), and MS95 is the nearest source for 32 elements. Against Palme & O'Neill 2014 (READ), 13 of 60 agree (Si, Ca, Cl, Co, Ti, V, Ge, Sc, Ce, Ag, Tl, Bi, Th). The tree's As = 18.5 ppm (stockgate.py:402) is exactly 10.000 times MS95's 1.85 ppm, which reads as a decimal slip made while transcribing MS95. The tree's N = 3180 ppm is exactly MS95's value; its P = 1040 ppm matches none of the three (L03 920, PON14 985, MS95 1080). So the table is a blend drawn mainly from MS95 and PON14, labelled L03. This is recorded, not repaired.

NORMALISATION (tree): stockgate.CHONDRITE sums to 1.006899 and is used without renormalising (stockgate.py:395-414, :545 DESTS 'CI chondrite': lambda: CHONDRITE). The effect on the factor is below 0.7%.

DROPPED: H2, the uncertainties. The tree carries each CI value as a point with no error (stockgate.py:395-414, stock.py:216-219), yet its binder conclusion ('binds on PHOSPHORUS, not nitrogen', stock.py:107-110; D25 via ledger.py:671-683) turns on CI N versus a crossover at N = P_CI*h_N/h_P = 2400 ppm at the tree's P. That crossover lies inside the 2-sigma band PON14 prints (2065-3835 ppm) and inside MS95's factor-of-2 band (1590-6360 ppm).

WEAKENED / OVERSTATED by the tree: stockgate.py:175-177 'A CI chondrite retained its volatiles, so like a star it binds on the least abundant required element'. The tree's own tables (stockgate.CHONDRITE against stockgate.solar_hybrid, per Si, by number) show CI N depleted 35 times, C 11 times and H about 5900 times relative to solar, while P, S and Zn sit near solar. What a CI chondrite retained is its moderately volatile elements; it lost most of its most-volatile ones. The binder argument needs only CI N/P (by mass) > payload N/P = 2.308. The tree values give 3.06, carried L03 gives 3.20, PON14 gives 2.99 and carried LBP25 gives 1.99. The last one fails.

ADDED by the tree (not a hypothesis of L03): 'CI composition represents the accessible stock of an asteroid destination' (stock.py:112 'THE OPTIMAL ARRIVAL NODE IS AN ASTEROID, NOT A PLANET'; stock.py:131-133). L03 averages five meteorite falls. That the bulk of a C-type asteroid has this composition and is accessible is a separate empirical claim. The obvious test (Ryugu and Bennu returned samples) could not be read here and is OPEN in this audit.

KEPT (qualitative): stock.py:107-108 'A chondrite never differentiated, so it still holds C, N, H, P and S together' matches the standard reading of CI chondrites as undifferentiated. The CI meteorites are aqueously altered, and Orgueil in particular is terrestrially weathered. That is not named in the tree, and its effect on H, S and N was not quantified here.

SUBSET (stock.py): stock.py:216-219 carries 16 of stockgate's 59 elements with identical values (checked). stock.py's factor 10.70096 (749.07 kg) differs from stockgate's 10.70115 (749.08 kg) only through the payload tables, not the chondrite.

(2) Attribution: within 0.5% the tree matches carried L03 on 7 of 39 elements, MS95 on 19 of 58 and PON14 on 13 of 60. As is exactly 10.000 times MS95. (3) Binder under each compilation, substituted into the tree table: TREE P 10.701, L03 P 12.097, MS95 P 10.305, PON14 P 11.299, LBP25 N 13.070. (4) sympy closed form: N binds iff N_CI < P_CI*h_N/h_P, which reproduces the 2400 ppm crossover at the tree's P. PON14's N 2-sigma band (2065-3835) spans the crossover. (5) The factor with P binding spans 10.305 to 12.097. (6) The craft binder stays Ta with a factor from 6.00e4 to 9.01e4. (7) From the tree's own tables, CI/solar per Si is N 0.0285, C 0.092, H 0.0002 and P 1.11, so 'retained its volatiles' overstates it.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. In 2003 Lodders lacked the post-2003 CI analyses: the revised N budget that LBP25 carries, modern ICP-MS/ID data, and the uncontaminated Ryugu and Bennu samples. EVIDENCE THAT THE MISSING DATA MOVE THINGS: CI N, the one datum the tree's binder label rests on, has moved from 2940 ppm (L03, carried) to 1965 ppm (LBP25, carried). That crosses the computed 2123-2400 ppm crossover and flips the tree's CI binder from P to N (factor 13.07, 914.9 kg, VOLATILITY-LIMITED). Independently, and using only data read here, PON14's 2014 2-sigma band for N (2065-3835 ppm) already spanned the crossover, and MS95 in 1995 flagged N as uncertain by a factor of 2. So the fragility was visible in the data, and it is the tree that dropped the uncertainty. EVIDENCE THAT THEY DO NOT: P moves by at most about 17% across four compilations (920-1080 ppm) and the rock-forming elements by about 3% or less. No verdict the tree draws (the stock need not travel; a primitive asteroid beats a planet by 33 to 42 times and cosmic gas by 146 to 185 times; the craft binds on Ta about 19 orders below the shell) moves under any compilation. Net: no datum Lodders lacked refutes the 2003 table. The most volatile element, N, was the least certain then and has moved since. The tree's binder label (P, ABUNDANCE-LIMITED) is sensitive to it, and the tree's table is not L03's in the first place.
grade_evidence: (i) This agent did not read L03 (NAMED-NOT-READ). So this audit neither confirms nor refutes any L03 number, and it makes no claim that Lodders is wrong. (ii) The tree's use of it is a CITED point table. That table is not L03 Table 3: against the carried L03 values 7 of 39 elements agree within 0.5%, against MS95 (READ) 19 of 58, and As is exactly 10 times MS95. This is an attribution and transcription discrepancy in the tree, and it is not a refutation. (iii) The conclusion the tree draws from the table, the CI binder = P at 10.70, moves with CI N. The sympy closed form puts the crossover at N_CI = P_CI*h_N/h_P, 2123 to 2492 ppm across compilations. PON14's own 2-sigma band (READ, no carried value used) spans it, MS95's factor-2 band spans it, and the 2025 value (carried, 1965 ppm) lies below it, flipping the binder to N at 13.07 and the regime label to VOLATILITY-LIMITED. A conclusion that moves with a moved and contested datum is DATA-DEPENDENT. (iv) It is not WRONG: no contradiction was computed against the source. It is not NARROWED as the primary grade, because every verdict (stock need not travel; asteroid over planet; site criterion, not a barrier) holds under all five compositions tested. (v) The tree's added hypothesis, that asteroid stock is CI-like and accessible, remains OPEN here because Ryugu and Bennu data could not be read.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: a settled CI N above about 2500 ppm with a band that clears the crossover. It would also need the tree to cite the composition it actually uses (MS95 and PON14 blend, not L03) and to carry the uncertainties. Toward NARROWED or re-graded: a read of the L03 primary (alphaXiv quota) confirming or correcting the carried Table 3 values. A read of LBP25's N uncertainty (+-970 vs +-447), which decides whether the flip is inside 1 sigma. Ryugu and Bennu bulk N and P, which bear on whether an asteroid destination is CI-like at all. To WRONG: only a computed contradiction in L03 at its own hypotheses, and none is claimed.
